about: Every number on these slides and in their speaker notes, with its source. All of them come from our evaluation tasks, measured on October 29, 2026. The learning page, site/content/learning.json, uses the same numbers.

claims.number: {{model:muse-glimmer-30b}}, unchanged, on a fresh 150-row test: exact match 93.3%, valid JSON 96.7%
claims.source: The base model’s scores in the published run record, on a fresh tool-call evaluation recorded before scoring.

claims.number: Frozen test: 150 rows over tool families held out of training
claims.source: Tessera’s continuous-tuning record: the test split holds the buckets and feeds tool families, pinned by digest, and training prompts only ever show other families. Each round also freezes a fresh holdout from the test families.

claims.number: {{model:muse-glimmer-30b}} with 63 training examples: +5.3 points on the frozen test, 95% CI 0.0 to +11.3; kept out
claims.source: The 63-row run on the frozen development test: exact match 87.3% to 92.7%, with 14 rows better and 6 worse. The paired bootstrap lower bound was not above zero, so the rule kept the base.

claims.number: {{model:muse-glimmer-30b}} with 511 training examples: +6.0 points on a fresh test (93.3% to 99.3%), 95% CI +2.0 to +10.7; 12 of 12 promotion-rule checks passed
claims.source: The 511-row run, scored on a fresh test built after training and recorded before scoring. The rule returned promote_candidate; nothing has been promoted or admitted.

claims.number: {{model:muse-glimmer-30b}}: exact match 93.3% to 99.3% on our 150-task tool-call evaluation, a fresh test, +6.0 points, 95% CI +2.0 to +10.7; 10 rows improved, 1 regressed
claims.source: QLoRA on Kaggle’s free notebook GPUs, October 29, 2026. The fresh test was built after training and recorded before scoring.

claims.number: {{model:muse-glimmer-30b}}: promotion rule 12 of 12 checks passed; a fresh reload matched 8 of 8 regenerated rows
claims.source: The rule, tool-call-specialist.promotion version 1, was fixed before scoring and returned promote_candidate. Nothing has been promoted or admitted, and the adapter weights are not published.

claims.number: {{model:muse-glimmer-30b}}: valid JSON 96.7% to 100.0%, correct refusals 97.3% to 99.3%; 0 test rows match the 511 training rows
claims.source: No exact, request-level or held-out-family match against the training rows. Against the older test set, 54 rows share only a request shape.

claims.number: {{model:muse-glimmer-30b}} on the frozen development test: 87.3% to 98.7%
claims.source: The test used while developing the runs. It served more than one run, so the fresh test is the one that decides.

claims.number: {{model:muse-glimmer-30b}}, as memory: closed-book exact match 0.0% to 62.5% on a 120-row test fixed before scoring, with 0 added tokens (+33.3 points vs a 222.3-token BM25 shim, 2.28 times faster, 8 of 8 reload check)
claims.source: QLoRA on two free Kaggle T4 GPUs, October 31, 2026: recalling the library’s Task Objects and multi-step workflows from the model’s own weights, with nothing added to the prompt. A promoted candidate only; nothing has been admitted or deployed.

claims.number: Memory, path-statistics and routing-weights learners: implemented and tested
claims.source: Tessera’s execution-learning record. Local tests are not evidence that any learner improves real work; that needs the evaluations each learner names, on real permitted runs.

claims.number: {{model:muse-glimmer-30b}} QLoRA on Kaggle’s two free T4 GPUs: 64 training steps in 83 minutes, on 511 rows
claims.source: The 511-row run record: 64 steps and 4,997.5 seconds of training, with each stage, library version and the peak memory of both GPUs recorded. The whole job took 8,789.5 seconds. The notebooks themselves are private.

claims.number: Another key tried to read everything the earlier tuning rounds wrote: all 303 reads were denied
claims.source: A final sweep after one model’s tuning rounds: another principal tried to read 115 private records, 133 blob chunks and 55 execution runs. After a second model’s rounds, all 193 such reads were denied too.
Tessera’s continuous-tuning record: with the disagreement these runs showed, a 150-row test detects a true 5-point gain only about 31% of the time, and 80% power needs about 560 rows.

claims.number: Self-learning library search with Herma shims, a local check: Recall@1 23.3% to 100.0% across 60 queries over 79 seed packs (MRR 0.341 to 1.000 in 1.0 round, 82.8% token reduction, 0.30 ms retrieval, 10 compiled shims at 0.026 ms, 10 of 10 independent reviews)
claims.source: An offline evaluation over the 79-pack library, with no model calls: each pack’s Task Objects enriched for search, an index across fields, reflection on misses, and an independent check (a self-approval was refused with a 409).
